keyVerseText: As I live, saith the LORD, though Coniah the son of Jehoiakim king of Judah were the signet upon my right hand, yet would I pluck thee thence;
rootMeaning: The name כׇּנְיָהוּ (Konyâhûw) is closely linked to its root form יְכׇנְיָה (Yᵉkonyâh), both meaning 'Jehovah will establish.' This etymology highlights a divine assurance of establishment or stability, which is profound given the historical context of the bearer. The literal sense conveys more than a mere personal name; it carries a theological declaration about God's sovereign role in establishing His people or their leaders.
usageInScripture: The term כׇּנְיָהוּ appears three times in Scripture, consistently referring to the Israelite king Jehoiachin, also known as Coniah. The translations vary slightly—'Coniah,' 'though Coniah,' and 'instead of Coniah'—indicating its function as a proper name but also emphasizing his significance in covenant history. This consistency underscores the name's identity as a marker of a pivotal king before Judah's captivity.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding כׇּנְיָהוּ as 'Jehovah will establish' invites reflection on God's sovereignty even in moments of judgment and exile. Though Jehoiachin was a king whose reign ended in captivity, his name reminds believers that God's ultimate purpose and establishment transcend human failure and political downfall. This name foreshadows the hope that God remains faithful to His covenant promises, a truth ultimately fulfilled in Christ, the eternal King who establishes an everlasting kingdom.
keyVerseReflection: Jeremiah 22:24 declares, 'though Coniah the son of Jehoiakim king of Judah were the signet upon my right hand, yet would I pluck thee thence.' Here, the use of כׇּנְיָהוּ (Coniah) as a signet—a symbol of authority and legitimacy—contrasts with God's judgment that will remove him despite his name's meaning. This tension highlights that divine establishment is not guaranteed by human status but by God's righteous will, reinforcing the seriousness of covenant faithfulness.
